definitions: Very small, narrow, and often unwanted polygons that can result from overlay operations in geographic information systems (GIS) or other computational geometry processes.
Residual polygons with disproportionately small area compared to their perimeter, typically indicative of data inaccuracies or processing artifacts.
examples: The GIS analysis generated numerous sliver polygons along the boundary.
Techniques exist to automatically detect and remove sliver polygons.
Careful data preparation can minimize the creation of sliver polygons.
